statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 17 because the Globex session has now held a 54-point band between 30,655.00 and 30,708.75 for 90 minutes without an extension attempt, after a cash session that retraced both its opening gap and its 30,235.67 low. Stress eases to 68 as WTI drifts to $89.16 following a 3.5% settle decline and the 30-year yield settles at 5.59% off a 5.62% intraday high that was still the highest since 2002.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the mapped state stays EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The published danger window remains narrow and sits on 30 September between 12:00Z and 15:00Z, where ADP, the August PCE deflators and the final Q2 GDP estimate precede the US cash open and Chicago PMI on quarter-end. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ has held 30,655.00-30,708.75 for 90 minutes at 30,683.50, up 0.23%, with ES in a matching 11-point band and VIX at 16.04, so Tail eases to 17; a 5.59% 30-year yield and 12-year-low consumer confidence hold Stress at 68
body:
The decisive current evidence is that the overnight session is holding a range rather than building a path. Ninety minutes after the 22:00Z reopen, NQ quotes 30,683.50, up 70.25 points or 0.23%, inside a session band of 30,655.00 to 30,708.75. That 53.75-point range is 0.18% of index level and contains no extension attempt. E-mini S&P futures corroborate it with an 11.25-point band between 7,738.00 and 7,749.25 at 7,743.75, up 0.15%. Two independent index futures holding narrow bands in parallel is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that Tail measures, and it is why Tail eases one point to 17.

The completed cash session supports the same reading. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,339.33, up 62.52 points or 0.21% from a 30,276.81 prior close. It opened at 30,412.29, printed a 30,429.97 high, sold through the prior close to a 30,235.67 low, then recovered 103.66 points to finish higher. Retracement worked in both directions: the opening gap was retraced and the downside probe was retraced in turn. VIX is 16.04, down 0.19% and near the low of a 15.73 to 16.44 range, which does not support a volatility-expansion regime.

Cross-asset evidence remains genuinely two-sided, which is why Stress stays high at 68 while Tail stays low. On the stressful side, the 30-year Treasury yield settled at 5.59%, up three basis points, after an intraday 5.62% that was the highest since 2002, and the 10-year settled at 5.26% inside a 5.21 to 5.29 range. Conference Board consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9 against an 89.2 consensus, the lowest since 2014, with the Expectations Index at 63.6 and average 12-month inflation expectations up to 6.1%. Job openings also came in below consensus near 7.1 million. On the relieving side, the front end eased: the 5-year settled at 5.06%, down about a basis point, and the 2-year fell to 4.88% from as high as 4.96% after New York Fed President Williams said there is no need for urgency on the next hike, which cut October hike odds to roughly 51% from 70%. That is a bear-steepening rather than a broad rate shock. WTI has drifted to $89.16 after settling $89.38, down 3.5%, as Saudi Arabia restored East-West pipeline capacity, Hormuz transit continued and up to 40 million barrels were released from emergency reserves. Gold at $4,215.70, up 0.86%, shows a mild hedge bid rather than an acute one.

Breadth is split rather than aligned. Fresh latest-session shared context, collected about 16 minutes before this assessment, showed three of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.68%, AAPL down 2.66% against META up 3.24%, and two-sided semiconductors where ARM rose 3.65% and MU rose 1.05% while QCOM fell 1.80%. Sector changes were narrow, with Technology up 0.14% and Consumer Cyclical down 0.13%. That context is delayed, latest-session and non-real-time with no source as-of, so it was used only as confirmation of split breadth and not as evidence of current NQ structure. Its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so futures and calendar conclusions rest entirely on directly verified sources. Under the contract, conflicting breadth reduces directional conviction and belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. Index performance diverged the same way, with the Nasdaq-100 up 0.21% while the Dow fell 0.26% to 51,349.92 and the S&P 500 fell 0.17% to 7,670.84.

No current amplifier stack is observed. There is no shallow-pullback pattern with repeated extension, NQ is not pinned at a session extreme, volatility is contained, the live oil input is easing on verified supply relief and the front end is repricing lower. Geopolitical transmission is easing rather than building on the evidence that matters here, namely the oil price itself. Tail therefore eases to 17 in the low band and the mapping produces EA_ON. Confidence holds 88 because current futures, index, volatility, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year yield, oil, gold, consumer-confidence, Fed-speaker and calendar evidence was verified directly this hour.

The published danger window stays narrow at 12:00Z to 15:00Z on 30 September, spanning ADP at 12:15Z, the August PCE deflators, personal income and spending and final Q2 GDP at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Chicago PMI at 13:45Z, on a quarter-end session. That stack is the only hour set where the forecast leaves the watch band, peaking at Tail 25 in the 13:00Z hour. It is a conditional scenario allowance for a delayed second leg meeting opening-auction continuation and concentrated rebalancing flow, not an assertion that such a path has formed.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on 29 September is unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 and never left the low or watch bands. It sat at 17 through the late Monday overnight, printed 24 in the 01:00, 03:00, 04:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on trend-down readings, held 20 to 21 through the European and US sessions, then eased to 19 and 18 after the US cash close. Stress fell steadily from 79 in the early Tuesday hours to 69 by 22:00 UTC as oil retreated and the front end repriced. Confidence stayed between 86 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The published forecast opens at Tail 17 for the current hour, where the 54-point Globex band and the resolved two-way cash path are actually observed, and holds 17 into the Asian handoff. It edges to 18 and then 19 across the Asian session as directly observed price-path evidence ages, enters the watch band at 20 with the European pre-open and reaches 21 around the European cash open. The conditional peak is the 13:00 UTC hour on 30 September at Tail 25, the only slot mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, where post-PCE price discovery would overlap the 13:30 UTC cash open, the 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI and quarter-end rebalancing. Tail then decays through the US afternoon to 20, ticks to 21 for the quarter-end power hour and cash close, and returns to the low band at 19 for the Globex reopen. Every forecast hour after the current one frames structure conditionally; no future price path or release outcome is treated as observed.
